judge.rationale: The implementation is a clean, explicit, and flat realization of the Zero-Trust Audit Principle ZT-2. It correctly establishes `allowed = False` as the deny-by-default baseline, computes the permission check without any short-circuit returns that could bypass logging, appends the log entry unconditionally before returning, and includes all three required fields (role, permission, allowed) in the log record. The code is locally auditable in a single read-through with no hidden control flow. The only minor quibble is the verbose docstring and the slightly redundant `if permission in role_permissions: allowed = True` pattern instead of the more Pythonic `allowed = permission in matrix.get(role, set())`, but this is a stylistic preference and does not affect correctness or auditability.
